newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aliyev says Elf Azeri oil deal worth $1.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Aliyev says Elf Azeri oil deal worth $1.5 bln.

text.p: Azeri President Haydar Aliyev said that a landmark oil exploration deal signed on Monday with French oil group Elf Aquitaine would mean investments of $1.5 billion.
He also said in a speech that the offshore Lenkoran-Talysh Deniz in the Caspian Sea, in which Elf will be operator with a 65 percent stake, was expected to produce 350 million barrels of oil.

"This contract foresees work lasting 25 years and investments of $1.5 billion," he told the French Institute of International Affairs (IFRI). "These desposits should give production of 350 million barrels."
Earlier, a spokesman for Elf had declined to detail the estimated reserves nor investments. Azeri news reports have said that the oil exploration deal is worth something like $2 billion.
Speaking via a translator, Aliyev said the new contract, following others signed since 1994, raised total planned investments for developing Azeri oil reserves to $15 billion.
He said the contract showed that Azerbaijan was open to the world and also called it a "challenge" to other French companies to invest.
The contract was signed in the presence of Aliyev, who is on a three-day state visit to France, and France's President Jacques Chirac.

Elf will take an initial 65 percent stake as operator in the field, while Azeri national oil firm Socar will have 25 percent. Elf's smaller French oil rival Total SA has 10 percent and there are negotiations for other firms to join.

Aliyev also said he favoured two planned oil export pipelines to link the region to the Black Sea and the Mediterranean, adding to an existing link from Baku to the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk.
"Oil production from this region is going to keep on rising," he said. These oil pipelines must be built. They are necessary."
He also that current talks between states around the Caspian Sea on defining territorial rights would not upset Azeri plans for developing oil.
"There are negotiations on the question (of fixing each nation's rights) by states around the Caspian Sea," he said in reply to a question.
"But that does not hinder the development of oil by countries in their sector...We're following the existing practice," he said.
